description:
Add an organization checker, or replace the one with the same name. A checker is the organization's own HTTPS endpoint that implements Valet's Checker API. Once saved, a release policy can run it as org:<name>: set_policy with that checker. Valet calls the endpoint's describe operation before saving and saves nothing if the call fails.

Saving a checker agrees, for the organization, to send the release files the endpoint asks for (the source, the build, or both) to the URL, for every release that a policy naming the checker evaluates. Once fetched, the files are outside Valet's control. Confirm that with the user before you call this tool. The answer names the files the endpoint asked for; those become the approved files. An endpoint that later asks for more is unavailable until the checker is saved again.

A credential header (Authorization, Cookie, X-Api-Key, or a name holding token, secret, key, or auth) takes exactly one {{NAME}} reference to a secret env var of the organization, after at most a scheme word, such as {"Authorization": "Bearer {{SNYK_TOKEN}}"}; any other text in it is refused. Valet resolves the reference at each call. Other headers are stored and listed as written. Have the user set the variable first with `valet env set SNYK_TOKEN=... --org <org>`, so the value never passes through this conversation. A reference to a variable that is not a secret of the organization is refused. list_policies shows the organization's checkers. Requires connecting a Valet account. Requires the Admin role.

checker.description: The checker's name, such as snyk. Policies name it org:snyk, and org:snyk is accepted here too. An existing name is replaced.

headers.description: Headers Valet sends on every call, as name to value. A credential header's value is one {{NAME}} reference to a secret env var of the organization, optionally after a scheme word, such as Bearer {{SNYK_TOKEN}}.

org_name.description: The Valet organization that owns the checker. Omit to use the organization the account joined first.

url.description: The endpoint's base URL, such as https://checks.example.com/snyk. Valet appends /v1/describe and so on. It is a public address.

name: set_checker

checker.description: The checker's name as a policy spells it, such as org:snyk. Pass it to set_policy as checker.

description.description: What the checker does, as the endpoint's describe operation reports it. Empty when the endpoint declares none.

display_name.description: The name a person reads, as the endpoint's describe operation reports it. Empty when the endpoint declares none.

fields.description: The settings a policy can give this checker, as the endpoint's describe operation reports them. Empty when it takes none.

description.description: What the setting is for. Empty when the checker gives none.

name.description: The setting's name, which set_policy takes as a key of settings.

required.description: True when a policy must give this setting.

secret.description: True when a person enters the value on a request page, not in settings.

headers.description: Headers Valet sends on every call, by name. A credential header shows its {{NAME}} reference, never a value. Empty when there are none.

inputs.description: The release files the endpoint asked for and this save approved: source, build, or both. Valet sends them to the URL for every release a policy naming this checker evaluates. Empty when it asked for none.

org.description: Name of the Valet organization the call acted in.

url.description: The endpoint's base URL as saved.

title: Add or replace an organization checker
